correctness.rationale: If the cubic sequence is binomid, k=1 yields integral f2/f1 and f3/f1. For ordered nonnegative integer a<=b<=c, u_t=(t+2)/(t+1) strictly decreases. Bounding 1<u_a u_b u_c excludes a>=3 and b outside 0..3,1..5,2..3. Solving exact integer m=f2/f1 via c+1=K/(m-K), K=u_a u_b, gives exactly twelve admissible triples and no unbounded c escapes. Independently enumerated all candidates using rational arithmetic and checked f3/f1, leaving exactly (0,0,0),(0,0,1),(0,1,2). Their sequences n³,2n·C2(n),6C3(n) are products/scalings of binomid integer n and Pascal columns; Shapiro’s integer determinant gives all generalized binomial coefficients integral. The package’s larger finite checks are corroboration, not an infinity argument. Carefully limited to cubic split-root shifts.
